classification.difficultyReason: Determine quarter-cycle points and periods for three explicitly specified sine functions, then coordinate their sketches on shared axes with excluded endpoints.

content.prompt: On the same set of axes, sketch the graphs of $y=\sin\theta$, $y=\sin 2\theta$ and $y=\sin 3\theta$ for $0^\circ<\theta<360^\circ$.

answer.short:
The three curves have amplitude $1$ and periods $360^\circ$, $180^\circ$ and $120^\circ$, respectively.

Use the sine curve's key points and repeat each curve at its period, as shown.
answer.worked:
For $y=\sin\theta$, plot the maximum $(90^\circ,1)$, zero $(180^\circ,0)$ and minimum $(270^\circ,-1)$.

For $y=\sin 2\theta$, plot maxima at $45^\circ,225^\circ$, minima at $135^\circ,315^\circ$, and zeros at $90^\circ,180^\circ,270^\circ$.

For $y=\sin 3\theta$, plot maxima at $30^\circ,150^\circ,270^\circ$, minima at $90^\circ,210^\circ,330^\circ$, and zeros at $60^\circ,120^\circ,180^\circ,240^\circ,300^\circ$.

Join each set of points with a smooth sine curve on the same axes. All three approach $0$ at both ends; $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$ are excluded.

spec.sourceRegion: Challenge exercise question 3; corroborating solution on teacher PDF page 89
spec.description: Three equation-driven sine curves on shared axes, distinguished by standard palette colours and line patterns. Open endpoints preserve the strict domain. No grid is supplied in the source.
spec.mathematics: Amplitude 1 throughout; periods 360, 180 and 120 degrees; curves sin(theta), sin(2theta), sin(3theta) on the open interval (0,360).
